# Taste
- Uses Typora as the visual benchmark for markdown-editor UI: wants the app's look (palette, typography, code-block styling) to closely match Typora, and supplies specific Typora themes (e.g. Inkwell) as references to replicate. Confidence: 0.7
- Objects to artificially capping the editor's content width; prefers width to behave like a real editor (responsive, growing with the window) rather than a fixed max-width. Confidence: 0.55
- Notices and cares about visual conflicts between UI elements — nested/double borders, margin collisions, background and font contrast clashes — and expects them treated as real defects. Confidence: 0.6
- For UI work, expects visual verification with actual screenshots and multimodal inspection of the rendered result, not just static code reasoning. Confidence: 0.6
- Wants the latest remote code pulled/synced before reviewing a codebase, to avoid reviewing stale code. Confidence: 0.5
- Writes in Chinese and expects responses/comments in Chinese. Confidence: 0.7
- Loses the thread when a reply bundles several independent technical threads with multiple open questions at once; expects plain-language explanations that separate the concerns and end with a single decision to make. Confidence: 0.4
- Favors a minimal, decluttered UI: content previews (formulas, diagrams) should be shown by default with editing behind an explicit action (progressive disclosure), prefers centered preview content, and wants a preview/read-only mode to stay distraction-free. In preview mode only the two states should exist — read-only preview and edit — with no sidebar, no session banner and no extra actions such as export. Confidence: 0.6
- Dislikes redundant UI labels and wasted space — wants superfluous text like a "预览" caption removed and the height it occupied reclaimed. Confidence: 0.55
- Prioritizes removing user friction (e.g. no directory-picker step, open a file by full path directly) over built-in safety scaffolding: explicitly asks that reads/writes go through native Node APIs rather than a permission-gated fs gateway, even if that drops grant checks and audit features. Confidence: 0.55
- Asks for a capability/gap assessment of the host or dependency project ("看看是否缺啥") before agreeing to an implementation, and welcomes being told which API gaps exist. Confidence: 0.5
- Prefers new features be implemented additively for the first cut: added as a separate/extra registration (e.g. a new agent tool) alongside the existing implementation, with the existing behavior left untouched rather than modified in place. Once the new path is settled, however, is willing to consolidate — asks to keep only the new tool and drop the superseded one, and expects the leftovers (dead helpers, i18n keys, stale comments) cleaned up. Confidence: 0.6
- Expects user-facing metadata and docs to be updated in lockstep with behavior changes: when a feature's I/O or permissions change, asks that the manifest description, safetyNotes, i18n strings and skill/changelog docs be reconciled so they describe the new reality. Confidence: 0.6
- When their local working copy and a shared/remote repo have diverged, prefers the local version to simply overwrite the repo version — treating their current state as the source of truth rather than carefully reconciling or reviewing the differences. Confidence: 0.5
- Expects release artifacts to be committed alongside the source change: when publishing a plugin, wants the packed package (and the regenerated catalog/index) committed in the same delivery, not left as a separate manual step. Confidence: 0.55
- In a shared multi-project repository, insists changes stay scoped to their own project — other projects' files and tests must not be touched. Confidence: 0.5
